upload-without-byte-route-01.graded_text: The design states that a file path or sandbox URI sent by a remote agent does not transfer the file's bytes, and the changed MCP tool no longer reads a caller-supplied path from the server's file system.

votes.e: A/project/docs/upload-design.md: "Wrong input shape. A remote server cannot accept a path from the caller's machine. No fix to path handling makes that work." and "The server can never see those paths." Code: A/project/packages/mcp/src/tools/upload-image.ts no longer imports node:fs; its header comment says "it cannot read paths on the caller's machine or sandbox, and it never handles image bytes itself". No tool takes a path input.

upload-without-byte-route-02.graded_text: The design gives each caller a route that moves bytes: the CLI reads local files and uploads them, HTTP clients send the bytes (multipart or a signed direct upload), and the remote MCP tool accepts a fetchable HTTPS URL or a host's documented file attachment reference.

votes.e: A/project/docs/upload-design.md: CLI "`kitepost upload <board_id> <file...>`: for each file, it stats the file ... calls create upload, PUTs the file from a stream, and calls finalize"; HTTP "The client PUTs the bytes to `put_url` with `put_headers`" (signed direct upload); MCP "`add_image_from_url` | `board_id`, `url` | An image already at a public `https://` URL. Kitepost fetches it." Implemented as addImageFromUrl in upload-image.ts:72-90.

upload-without-byte-route-03.graded_text: When an MCP caller has no supported byte route, the tool returns an explicit error that names the routes that do work, and the changed tool code cannot report success unless validated bytes were stored (the empty-buffer success path is gone).

votes.e: Half holds: success only comes from toResult on an ok Outcome<Image> (upload-image.ts:61-66), and the empty-buffer path is gone. The no-route error does not exist, though. The guidance for a caller with no byte route appears only in a tool description: upload-image.ts:17-18 NO_ROUTE_HINT "If you cannot make an HTTP request from where the file is, tell the user ... drop it onto the board in the Kitepost app", which is concatenated into createImageUpload.description (line 98) and never returned. The 412 input `/mnt/data/photo.jpg` sent as `url` fails `z.string().url()` (line 81-83) with a generic schema error. The retired `upload_image` returns "an unknown-tool error" (design, Decisions 3). A no-network caller who follows create_image_upload gets back only upload_missing_bytes: "No file has arrived for this upload yet. PUT the file to put_url ..." (line 53). None of these names a route that works for that caller.

upload-without-byte-route-04.graded_text: Inline base64 or other inline content through the model is either refused or capped at a stated small size, so a multi-megabyte photo is never routed through model context.

votes.e: A/project/docs/upload-design.md Principles: "No inline or base64 bytes on any surface (see \"Decisions\" for 421)." Decisions 1: "No base64 or inline input, even for small images." Tool descriptions say "Do not send base64" (upload-image.ts:98). The "separate tool with a hard cap of about 64 KB" is offered only as an option for later and is not part of the design.

upload-without-byte-route-05.graded_text: If the server fetches any URL, including one a host gives for an attachment, the design names enforced limits: blocking private and internal addresses, a redirect limit with each hop rechecked, a streamed size cap at the product's file limit, a timeout, and validation of the actual bytes or type. It never describes URL input as unbounded.

votes.e: A/project/docs/upload-design.md importFromUrl: "`https:` only. Resolve DNS and refuse loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, and cloud metadata addresses. Re-check on every redirect, with at most 3 redirects." "Timeout of 20 s. Stream the body and abort once it passes 20 MB." "Check the type again by magic number on the bytes received."

upload-without-byte-route-06.graded_text: Nothing in the design changes the browser's drag-and-drop flow, and the design states that every route it defines ends in the same authorization, quota, validation, and finalize step the browser flow uses before an image counts as added.

votes.e: A/project/docs/upload-design.md: "Bytes go straight to object storage ... This is the flow the browser app already uses, and it works." "Every surface uses one product capability, with the same authorization, limits, and quota. The MCP server, HTTP API, CLI, and browser app are thin adapters over it." "An upload counts as done only after finalize checks the stored object." importFromUrl: "then run the same finalize steps." Nothing proposes changing drag-and-drop.

upload-without-byte-route-07.graded_text: Upload staging and completion stay in the HTTP API and CLI: an agent that can run commands is pointed at the CLI or HTTP upload, and the MCP catalog gains no separate tools for starting, signing, or finalizing an upload.

votes.e: A/project/docs/upload-design.md MCP table adds "`create_image_upload` ... Returns a signed `put_url`" and "`finalize_image_upload` | `upload_id` | After the PUT." These are implemented as createImageUpload and finalizeImageUpload in upload-image.ts:92-150 and exported in `imageUploadTools = [addImageFromUrl, createImageUpload, finalizeImageUpload]` (line 152). That puts staging, signing, and finalizing in the MCP catalog, and the 418 coding agent is routed to them instead of to the CLI.

blocking: [opus-for-opus2] The MCP catalog gains upload staging and finalize tools: upload-image.ts:152 `export const imageUploadTools = [addImageFromUrl, createImageUpload, finalizeImageUpload];`. The design's 418 flow is "`create_image_upload` → `curl -X PUT --data-binary @chart.png ...` from the sandbox shell → `finalize_image_upload`". This turns a CLI/HTTP workflow into a three-call MCP protocol, and the signed write URL lands in model context and transcripts. The design concedes this: "The URL appears in the model's context and transcript."

[opus-for-opus2] Quota race under concurrency. createUpload only checks quota ("Quota: the account's used storage plus `sizeBytes` fits the plan limit"), and usage is charged later at finalize ("Mark the row `ready`, attach the image to the board, and **then** charge storage usage."). Nothing reserves the space, and finalize never rechecks quota. N parallel createUpload calls near the 2 GB limit all pass the check, and all of them finalize. (docs/upload-design.md)

[opus-for-opus2] No caller with a dead byte route ever receives an error naming a working route. NO_ROUTE_HINT exists only inside createImageUpload.description (upload-image.ts:17-18, 98). A 412-style `url: "/mnt/data/photo.jpg"` fails `z.string().url()` with a generic validation error (upload-image.ts:81-83). The retired `upload_image` returns an unknown-tool error (design Decisions 3).
